headline: India's grid planners are warning that the data center boom is straining the power system and raising the cost of upgrading it.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a well-sourced look at grid worries from official meeting minutes, but the picture is mixed and no outage is reported.
importance_line: Electricity users and state utilities in India could face higher grid-upgrade bills and less stable supply near data-center hubs, but an industry body says the extra demand is manageable and operators should pay for their own connections.
summary: The Hindu reports, from regional power committee minutes it reviewed, that the estimated cost of upgrading grid control systems in India's north-east has risen from about 5.2 billion to 6.9 billion rupees because AI-driven demand is making the hardware dearer. The minutes also show grid bodies warning that data centers can swing demand sharply or switch suddenly to backup power, while the director general of the All-India Discoms Association, an industry body, says growth of one to two gigawatts a year is manageable, though local transmission upgrades could be hard in crowded cities.
notes: Rs 521 crore = 5.21 billion rupees; Rs 688 crore = 6.88 billion rupees. Published 10 Oct 2026 (19:11 IST).
